title: Every Student, Every Family
answer: Part III, Every Student, Every Family, covers special education and accessibility, English learners and newcomers, communication with families, wellbeing and safety, and counseling and college. These chapters address the students and families who most need careful attention.

children.name: Special Education and Accessibility
children.blurb: A review of research on AI with students with disabilities found something uncomfortable. Much of the work described AI as a way to relieve adults of the burden of working with these students, rather than as a way to empower the students and their families (Rice, 2023).

children.name: English Learners and Newcomers
children.blurb: In a trial with 217 second graders learning English, most of them Latino, a computer tutor taught the vocabulary of science and social studies units. Students who used it learned more of the taught words than students who did not, with an effect of 0.38 (Baker et al., 2020).

children.name: Communicating With Families
children.blurb: A school district once had a problem with truancy notices. The letters sent to families were written in legal language, warning of consequences and citing the education code.

children.name: Wellbeing, Behavior, Attendance, and Safety
children.blurb: A study of 14 companies that monitor students online found that most watch students around the clock, not just during school hours. Most use AI to flag concerning content, but fewer than half described any human review of those flags.

children.name: Counseling, College, and Career
children.blurb: Every spring, many high school graduates are admitted to college, plan to go, and never show up in the fall. Researchers call this summer melt.

sections.body: This part of school life is the work schools do with students and families who most need careful attention. It covers special education and accessibility, English learners and newcomers, communication with families, wellbeing and safety, and counseling and college. The book describes AI in this part through randomized trials that involve messages to families and support for students after high school. These five chapters sit together because they address the same group of students and families, and they carry some of the strongest evidence in the Volume. The book gives this part careful weight because these are the students and families who most need careful attention.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The book finds that this part holds some of the strongest evidence in the Volume, including several randomized trials about messages to families and support for students after high school. It also finds some of its firmest rules here, especially rules about decisions that must stay with people. What does not work, in the book's view, is letting AI take over those decisions. The rule it holds to is that decisions that must stay with people do stay with people, and the book treats that as firm. The book does not present these areas as places where AI should replace people in decisions.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The five pages fit together as the chapters of this Part, each taking one part of the same concern for students and families who most need careful attention. A teacher would go to Special Education and Accessibility for special education and accessibility, and to English Learners and Newcomers for English learners and newcomers. A leader would go to Communicating With Families for communication with families, and to Wellbeing, Behavior, Attendance, and Safety for wellbeing and safety. A parent would go to Counseling, College, and Career for counseling and the path after high school. Across all five, the book points to strong evidence and to firm rules about decisions that must stay with people.
